overview_markdown:
PalmClaw is an open-source, EMNLP 2026 demo agent framework explicitly inspired by OpenClaw but re-architected to run natively on Android phones. Instead of requiring a PC or server, it keeps sessions, context management, memory, skills, tools, and the agent loop entirely on the device, while delegating model inference to a user-configured LLM API. It ships as a downloadable APK with 769 tests and active development through v0.3.1.

Its distinguishing features are mobile-native structured device tools and a control-oriented security model: actions are gated by schemas, permissions, confirmations, and workspace boundaries. Recent commits show work on MCP client lifecycle hardening, always-on reliability, and provider endpoint compatibility, suggesting a push toward robustness.

Compared to OpenClaw, PalmClaw trades ecosystem breadth and multi-channel reach for true on-phone operation and a low-friction install. It is best viewed as an early-stage, research-grade mobile alternative rather than a production-ready replacement.
